cases.title: Low free T3 and a borderline TSH in a ventilated patient with septic shock

cases.summary: Non-thyroidal illness syndrome mimicking central hypothyroidism, resolved by reverse T3 and by the TSH rebound during recovery. The case exists to punish reflexive levothyroxine prescribing in intensive care.

summary_i18n.en: Non-thyroidal illness syndrome mimicking central hypothyroidism; resolved by reverse T3 and the recovery-phase TSH rebound.
summary_i18n.de: Non-Thyroidal-Illness-Syndrom als Imitat einer zentralen Hypothyreose; geklärt durch reverses T3 und den TSH-Rebound in der Erholungsphase.
summary_i18n.es: Síndrome del enfermo eutiroideo que simula hipotiroidismo central; se resuelve con la T3 reversa y el rebote de TSH en la recuperación.
summary_i18n.nl: Non-thyroidal illness syndroom dat centrale hypothyreoïdie nabootst; opgelost door reverse T3 en de TSH-rebound in de herstelfase.
summary_i18n.ru: Синдром нетиреоидных заболеваний, имитирующий центральный гипотиреоз; разрешён по реверсивному Т3 и «рикошету» ТТГ в фазе восстановления.

cases.author: MedSimQA Editorial

presentation.chief_complaint: Day 4 of mechanical ventilation for faecal peritonitis and septic shock; thyroid function tests ordered by the night team after a nurse queried the patient's low temperature.

chief_complaint_i18n.en: Day 4 of ventilation for faecal peritonitis and septic shock; thyroid function tests ordered overnight.
chief_complaint_i18n.de: Tag 4 der Beatmung bei kotiger Peritonitis und septischem Schock; Schilddrüsenwerte nachts angefordert.
chief_complaint_i18n.es: Cuarto día de ventilación por peritonitis fecaloidea y shock séptico; función tiroidea solicitada de madrugada.
chief_complaint_i18n.nl: Dag 4 van beademing wegens faecale peritonitis en septische shock; schildklierfunctie 's nachts aangevraagd.
chief_complaint_i18n.ru: 4-е сутки ИВЛ по поводу калового перитонита и септического шока; функция щитовидной железы назначена ночной сменой.

presentation.history_of_present_illness: Emergency Hartmann procedure for a perforated sigmoid diverticulum. Postoperatively he required noradrenaline at 0.28 µg/kg/min, continuous veno-venous haemofiltration for anuric acute kidney injury, and lung-protective ventilation for a moderate ARDS. He received a single 200 mg dose of intravenous hydrocortisone at induction and a 5-day course of dopamine at a renal dose on another unit before transfer. He is sedated with propofol and fentanyl. No known thyroid disease, no thyroid medication, and no cranial trauma or pituitary history.

medications.name: Dopamine
medications.notes: Directly suppresses TSH secretion; a documented confounder for this exact test.

medications.name: Hydrocortisone
medications.notes: Glucocorticoids suppress TSH and inhibit T4-to-T3 conversion.

review_of_systems.note: Sedated and ventilated; systems review not obtainable

examination_findings: Sedated, RASS -4, ventilated on FiO2 0.55, PEEP 12
No goitre, no lid lag, no proptosis
No stigmata of pituitary disease: no visual field defect assessable, no gynaecomastia, no loss of body hair

lab_panels.comment: Day 4 of critical illness. This is the pattern that generates inappropriate levothyroxine prescriptions.

results.interference_note: Low but not suppressed. Dopamine and glucocorticoid both suppress TSH directly; neither implies pituitary disease.
The dominant abnormality. Low T3 is the earliest and most consistent feature of non-thyroidal illness syndrome, driven by reduced type 1 deiodinase and increased type 3 deiodinase activity.

THE discriminator. Reverse T3 is HIGH in non-thyroidal illness (T4 is shunted down the inactivating pathway) and LOW or normal in true central hypothyroidism, where there is simply less T4 to metabolise.

lab_panels.comment: Ordered because the TFT pattern superficially resembles central hypothyroidism.

results.interference_note: An appropriately high stress cortisol effectively excludes global anterior pituitary failure. A cortisol of 782 nmol/L in shock is a working corticotroph axis.
Mildly raised - stress and dopamine antagonism, not a prolactinoma.
Suppressed gonadotrophins are near-universal in critical illness and must not be read as hypopituitarism.
Severe hypoalbuminaemia depresses measured free T4 on analogue immunoassays; some of the low FT4 here is analytical rather than physiological.

lab_panels.comment: Recovery phase: extubated day 16, vasopressors stopped day 12, off filtration. No thyroid hormone was ever given.

results.interference_note: The recovery-phase TSH rebound. This transient overshoot is diagnostic of resolving non-thyroidal illness and is routinely misread as newly diagnosed hypothyroidism, leading to lifelong and unnecessary levothyroxine.

lab_panels.comment: Outpatient follow-up six weeks after discharge. Never treated.

imaging.findings: Normal pituitary height (6 mm) and homogeneous enhancement. No adenoma, no haemorrhage, no empty sella, no stalk thickening. Optic chiasm normal.
imaging.impression: Normal pituitary. Performed only because the day-4 pattern raised the question of central hypothyroidism; in retrospect the reverse T3 had already answered it and this scan added cost without information.

protocols.name: Supportive management of non-thyroidal illness syndrome (no thyroid hormone)

name_i18n.en: Supportive management of non-thyroidal illness syndrome (no thyroid hormone)
name_i18n.es: Manejo de soporte del síndrome del enfermo eutiroideo (sin hormona tiroidea)
name_i18n.nl: Ondersteunende behandeling van non-thyroidal illness syndroom (geen schildklierhormoon)
name_i18n.ru: Поддерживающая тактика при синдроме нетиреоидных заболеваний (без гормонов щитовидной железы)

protocols.guideline_source: Composite critical-care endocrinology practice; no guideline supports routine thyroid hormone in NTIS
protocols.indication: Low T3 pattern in critical illness with a raised reverse T3 and no antecedent thyroid disease.

regimen.notes: Randomised trials of T3 or T4 replacement in NTIS have not shown mortality benefit and T4 supplementation may worsen outcome by suppressing the adaptive response.
Source control, appropriate antimicrobials, organ support.
Dopamine and high-dose glucocorticoid both suppress TSH; both had been given here.

monitoring: Do not repeat thyroid function tests during the acute phase - they will remain abnormal and generate pressure to treat
Repeat TSH and FT4 at least 6 weeks after clinical recovery, as an outpatient
If the recovery TSH exceeds 20 mIU/L or FT4 remains low at 6 weeks, then reassess for genuine thyroid disease
Measure reverse T3 only where central hypothyroidism is a genuine consideration; it is a send-away assay and rarely changes management otherwise
contraindications: Thyroid hormone replacement is contraindicated in the absence of evidence of true hypothyroidism
adverse_effects: Iatrogenic thyrotoxicosis, arrhythmia and increased myocardial oxygen demand if levothyroxine is given inappropriately
protocols.notes: The single most important intervention in this case was not ordering the test on day 4. Thyroid function testing in the acute phase of critical illness has a very low pre-test probability of changing management and a high probability of causing harm through misinterpretation.

diagnoses.label: Non-thyroidal illness syndrome (euthyroid sick syndrome)
diagnoses.discriminator: Raised reverse T3 with a low FT3, an intact cortisol response, and complete spontaneous normalisation through a transient TSH rebound - none of which occurs in central hypothyroidism.
supporting_evidence: FT3 1.9 pmol/L as the dominant abnormality with a proportionally smaller FT4 fall
Random cortisol 782 nmol/L - corticotroph axis intact
CRP 284 mg/L and albumin 18 g/L - severe systemic inflammation
Documented dopamine and glucocorticoid exposure, both TSH-suppressing
Recovery-phase TSH rebound to 8.4 mIU/L followed by full normalisation at 90 days without treatment

diagnoses.label: Central (secondary) hypothyroidism
diagnoses.discriminator: Reverse T3 is raised, not low; cortisol is appropriately high; the pituitary MRI is normal; and the axis normalised spontaneously. Any one of these argues against central hypothyroidism, and together they exclude it.
supporting_evidence: Low FT4 with a non-elevated TSH is the textbook pattern of central hypothyroidism

diagnoses.label: Drug-induced TSH suppression (dopamine, glucocorticoid)

label_i18n.es: Supresión de TSH inducida por fármacos

diagnoses.discriminator: A genuine contributing mechanism rather than a competing diagnosis; it explains why the TSH was 0.28 rather than the mildly raised value that would otherwise be expected.

diagnoses.label: Primary hypothyroidism
diagnoses.discriminator: TSH was low, not high, at presentation. The day-21 TSH of 8.4 mIU/L is the classic point at which this wrong diagnosis gets made.

teaching_points: Reverse T3 is the discriminator between non-thyroidal illness syndrome and central hypothyroidism: it is HIGH in the former and LOW-to-normal in the latter. Nothing else in the routine panel separates them reliably.

The recovery-phase TSH rebound is a normal part of resolving critical illness. A TSH of 5-20 mIU/L in the week after extubation is expected, and treating it commits the patient to lifelong replacement for a condition they never had.

Do not order thyroid function tests in the acute phase of critical illness unless thyroid disease is genuinely suspected as a contributor. The test will be abnormal, and the abnormality will be misleading.
Severe hypoalbuminaemia depresses free T4 on analogue immunoassays. Part of the low FT4 here is analytical artefact from an albumin of 18 g/L, not reduced hormone availability.

Suppressed gonadotrophins, a mildly raised prolactin and a low testosterone are near-universal in critical illness. Reading them as hypopituitarism produces a cascade of unnecessary imaging - as the normal MRI in this case demonstrates.
An appropriately high random cortisol during shock is strong evidence against global anterior pituitary failure and is the cheapest test that reframes this whole panel.

references.citation: Fliers E, Boelen A. An update on non-thyroidal illness syndrome. J Endocrinol Invest 2021.
Van den Berghe G. Non-thyroidal illness in the ICU: a syndrome with different faces. Thyroid 2014.

must_include_findings.label: Low free T3 as the dominant abnormality

expected_next_tests: pituitary mri only if the axis fails to normalise

safety_rules.description: Must not recommend levothyroxine or liothyronine for this pattern.
Should recommend deferring reassessment until after clinical recovery.

cases.title: Thyrotoxicosis five months after starting amiodarone: type 1 or type 2?

title_i18n.en: Thyrotoxicosis five months after starting amiodarone: type 1 or type 2?
title_i18n.de: Thyreotoxikose fünf Monate nach Amiodaron-Beginn: Typ 1 oder Typ 2?
title_i18n.es: Tirotoxicosis cinco meses tras iniciar amiodarona: ¿tipo 1 o tipo 2?
title_i18n.nl: Thyreotoxicose vijf maanden na start amiodaron: type 1 of type 2?
title_i18n.ru: Тиреотоксикоз через пять месяцев после начала приёма амиодарона: тип 1 или тип 2?

cases.summary: Amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis in a patient who cannot safely stop the drug. The case turns on separating iodine-induced hyperfunction (type 1) from destructive thyroiditis (type 2), because the treatments are opposite and the wrong one wastes months.

summary_i18n.en: Amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis where type 1 and type 2 demand opposite treatments; Doppler and the steroid response settle it.
summary_i18n.de: Amiodaron-induzierte Thyreotoxikose, bei der Typ 1 und Typ 2 gegensätzliche Therapien erfordern; Doppler und Steroidansprechen entscheiden.
summary_i18n.es: Tirotoxicosis por amiodarona en la que el tipo 1 y el tipo 2 exigen tratamientos opuestos; el Doppler y la respuesta a corticoides lo resuelven.
summary_i18n.nl: Amiodaron-geïnduceerde thyreotoxicose waarbij type 1 en type 2 tegengestelde behandelingen vergen; doppler en steroïdrespons geven uitsluitsel.
summary_i18n.ru: Амиодарон-индуцированный тиреотоксикоз, при котором тип 1 и тип 2 требуют противоположного лечения; вопрос решают допплер и ответ на стероиды.

cases.author: MedSimQA Editorial

presentation.chief_complaint: Recurrence of palpitations and 6 kg weight loss five months after amiodarone was started for recurrent ventricular tachycardia.

chief_complaint_i18n.en: Recurrent palpitations and 6 kg weight loss five months after starting amiodarone.
chief_complaint_i18n.de: Erneute Palpitationen und 6 kg Gewichtsverlust fünf Monate nach Amiodaron-Beginn.
chief_complaint_i18n.es: Palpitaciones recurrentes y pérdida de 6 kg cinco meses después de iniciar amiodarona.
chief_complaint_i18n.nl: Terugkerende palpitaties en 6 kg gewichtsverlies vijf maanden na start van amiodaron.
chief_complaint_i18n.ru: Возобновление сердцебиения и потеря 6 кг веса через пять месяцев после начала приёма амиодарона.

presentation.history_of_present_illness: Amiodarone was started after an episode of sustained monomorphic ventricular tachycardia in the context of ischaemic cardiomyopathy with an ejection fraction of 28%. He has an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator. Baseline thyroid function before amiodarone was normal (TSH 1.8 mIU/L, FT4 15.1 pmol/L) and is documented in the record - a detail without which this case would be far harder. Over the last six weeks he has lost weight, become tremulous and heat-intolerant, and his device has recorded three episodes of non-sustained ventricular tachycardia after four quiet months. The cardiology team's position is that stopping amiodarone risks a life-threatening arrhythmia.
past_medical_history: Sustained monomorphic VT with ICD in situ

medications.name: Amiodarone
medications.notes: Each 200 mg tablet contains about 75 mg of iodine, of which 6-9 mg is released daily - roughly 40 times the recommended daily intake. Half-life is 50-100 days, so the iodine load persists for months after stopping.

presentation.social_history: Ex-smoker. No alcohol. Lives with his daughter.

review_of_systems.cardiovascular: Palpitations, three ICD-recorded NSVT episodes, worsening exertional dyspnoea
review_of_systems.general: 6 kg weight loss, heat intolerance, tremor
review_of_systems.ophthalmic: No grittiness, no diplopia, no proptosis

examination_findings: No orbitopathy, no lid retraction, no proptosis
Fine tremor of the outstretched hands
Bibasal crackles, JVP 4 cm, mild ankle oedema
Corneal microdeposits on slit lamp (an expected amiodarone finding, not thyroid-related)
Slate-grey skin discolouration over the malar area

lab_panels.comment: Presentation. Compare with the documented pre-amiodarone baseline TSH 1.8, FT4 15.1.

results.interference_note: Note the very high FT4 with a comparatively modest FT3 rise: amiodarone blocks type 1 deiodinase, so T4-to-T3 conversion is impaired even during thyrotoxicosis.
Raised by deiodinase blockade, not by illness. Reverse T3 cannot be used to argue for non-thyroidal illness in a patient on amiodarone.

lab_panels.comment: Ordered specifically to exclude coincidental Graves disease, which amiodarone can unmask.

results.interference_note: Negative. Rules out Graves disease as the mechanism, which would otherwise have been a treatable third possibility.
Markedly raised, consistent with follicular destruction and release of stored colloid - supports type 2.
Raised in destructive (type 2) disease. The literature on IL-6 as a discriminator is inconsistent and it should support, never drive, the decision.
Massive iodine load confirming amiodarone exposure. This also explains why radioiodine is not an option: the gland will not take up tracer against this iodine background.

lab_panels.comment: Two weeks on prednisolone 40 mg daily. Carbimazole 40 mg was given concurrently for the first 10 days while the type was uncertain, then withdrawn.

results.interference_note: A fall of 20 pmol/L in 14 days. This magnitude and speed of response to glucocorticoid alone is itself diagnostic of type 2; type 1 does not behave this way.

lab_panels.comment: Six weeks; prednisolone tapering by 10 mg every two weeks. Amiodarone continued throughout on cardiology advice.
Four months; prednisolone stopped at week 12. Amiodarone continued.

results.interference_note: The hypothyroid tail of destructive thyroiditis. Type 2 amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis not uncommonly ends in permanent hypothyroidism; this needs monitoring, not alarm.

imaging.findings: Normal-sized gland (14 mL), mildly heterogeneous echotexture, no nodules. Colour flow pattern 0 (Bogazzi classification): absent intraparenchymal vascularity. Inferior thyroid artery peak systolic velocity 14 cm/s (reduced).
imaging.impression: Absent vascularity in a non-goitrous gland. Combined with a raised thyroglobulin and negative TRAb, this indicates destructive (type 2) amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis rather than iodine-induced hyperfunction (type 1), in which vascularity is normal or increased and nodules are usually present.

imaging.findings: Absent thyroidal sestamibi retention on delayed images.
imaging.impression: Absent retention supports type 2 (destroyed, metabolically inactive follicles). Sestamibi is used because conventional pertechnetate or radioiodine uptake is uninterpretable against an iodine load of this magnitude.

imaging.findings: LVEF 24% (down from 28%), moderate functional mitral regurgitation, no thrombus.
imaging.impression: Thyrotoxicosis-related deterioration in an already severely impaired ventricle. Establishes the urgency of biochemical control.

protocols.name: High-dose glucocorticoid for type 2 amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis with amiodarone continuation

name_i18n.en: High-dose glucocorticoid for type 2 amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis
name_i18n.de: Hochdosierte Glukokortikoide bei Amiodaron-induzierter Thyreotoxikose Typ 2
name_i18n.es: Glucocorticoides a dosis altas para tirotoxicosis por amiodarona tipo 2
name_i18n.nl: Hooggedoseerde glucocorticoïden bij amiodaron-geïnduceerde thyreotoxicose type 2
name_i18n.ru: Высокодозная глюкокортикоидная терапия при амиодарон-индуцированном тиреотоксикозе 2-го типа

protocols.guideline_source: ETA 2018 guideline on amiodarone-induced thyroid dysfunction (adapted)
protocols.indication: Type 2 amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis in a patient with severe left ventricular impairment in whom amiodarone withdrawal carries an unacceptable arrhythmic risk.

regimen.notes: Anti-inflammatory action on the destructive thyroiditis. A clear FT4 fall within 2-4 weeks both treats and confirms type 2.
Total course 12 weeks. Too rapid a taper causes rebound thyrotoxicosis.
Given empirically while the type was uncertain (a legitimate 'treat both' strategy in an unstable patient), then withdrawn once the Doppler and steroid response established type 2.

Continued after multidisciplinary discussion. Stopping it would not have helped acutely - the 50-100 day half-life means the iodine load persists for months - and the arrhythmic risk was judged higher than the thyroid risk.
Rate control and symptom relief; dose limited by the low blood pressure and poor ventricular function.

monitoring: FT4 and FT3 every 2 weeks during the acute phase - the rate of FT4 fall is the diagnostic readout, not just a progress marker
Capillary glucose while on prednisolone: he is at high risk of steroid-induced hyperglycaemia
Repeat echocardiography once euthyroid to reassess ejection fraction
TSH and FT4 every 3 months indefinitely while amiodarone continues, and after stopping it for at least 12 months
Watch specifically for the hypothyroid tail, which appeared here at four months
contraindications: Radioiodine is not usable: the iodine load abolishes tracer uptake
Thionamides alone are ineffective in pure type 2 - the gland is not synthesising hormone, it is leaking it
adverse_effects: Steroid-induced hyperglycaemia, fluid retention (a real problem with LVEF 24%), gastric ulceration, mood disturbance, and opportunistic infection
Rebound thyrotoxicosis if the taper is too fast
Permanent hypothyroidism as a sequel of the destructive process
protocols.notes: Mixed or indeterminate forms are common and it is legitimate to treat both mechanisms at once in an unstable patient, then withdraw the arm that is not working. Total thyroidectomy under local or regional anaesthesia remains the definitive option for refractory disease with cardiac decompensation, and should be considered early rather than as a last resort in a failing ventricle.

diagnoses.label: Type 2 amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis (destructive thyroiditis)
diagnoses.discriminator: Absent Doppler vascularity in a non-nodular gland, raised thyroglobulin, negative TRAb, absent sestamibi retention, and a 20 pmol/L fall in FT4 within two weeks of glucocorticoid alone.
supporting_evidence: Colour flow pattern 0 with reduced peak systolic velocity
Rapid response to prednisolone with FT4 48.2 to 28.4 pmol/L in 14 days
Subsequent hypothyroid phase at four months, characteristic of a destructive process

diagnoses.label: Type 1 amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis (iodine-induced hyperfunction)
diagnoses.discriminator: Type 1 arises on a pre-existing abnormal gland (nodular goitre or latent Graves), shows normal or increased vascularity, and responds to thionamides plus potassium perchlorate rather than to steroids.
supporting_evidence: Massive iodine load is present in both types
refuting_evidence: Carbimazole withdrawal made no difference to the trajectory

diagnoses.label: Coincidental Graves disease unmasked by iodine (Jod-Basedow)

label_i18n.en: Coincidental Graves disease unmasked by iodine
label_i18n.es: Enfermedad de Graves coincidente desenmascarada por yodo
label_i18n.nl: Toevallige ziekte van Graves ontmaskerd door jodium

diagnoses.discriminator: Negative TRAb with absent vascularity and no goitre or orbitopathy.

diagnoses.label: Mixed/indeterminate amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis

label_i18n.es: Tirotoxicosis por amiodarona mixta o indeterminada

diagnoses.discriminator: Cannot be formally excluded at presentation, which is precisely why dual therapy for the first ten days was reasonable. The steroid-alone response after carbimazole withdrawal argues against a significant type 1 component.
supporting_evidence: Both mechanisms can coexist and the discriminators are imperfect
refuting_evidence: Continued improvement after carbimazole was stopped

teaching_points: The two types of amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis require opposite treatments: thionamides (with or without potassium perchlorate) for type 1, glucocorticoids for type 2. Guessing wrongly costs weeks in a patient whose heart cannot afford them.
Absent colour Doppler vascularity is the most useful single bedside discriminator. A hypervascular gland is type 1; an avascular one is type 2.

Stopping amiodarone does not produce a rapid improvement. Its half-life is 50-100 days and the iodine load persists for months, so withdrawal is a decision about future arrhythmia risk, not about acute thyroid control.
Radioiodine is unusable in this setting: the iodine load competes out the tracer. Sestamibi scintigraphy is the workable nuclear alternative.

Amiodarone blocks type 1 deiodinase, so free T4 and reverse T3 rise disproportionately to free T3. Reverse T3 therefore cannot be used to argue for non-thyroidal illness in a patient taking amiodarone.
A documented pre-treatment thyroid function test transforms the interpretability of this presentation. Baseline TSH and FT4 before starting amiodarone should be treated as mandatory.
Type 2 disease frequently ends in hypothyroidism. Surveillance must continue after the thyrotoxicosis resolves - this patient needed levothyroxine four months later.

references.citation: Bartalena L et al. 2018 ETA Guidelines for the Management of Amiodarone-Associated Thyroid Dysfunction. Eur Thyroid J.
Bogazzi F et al. Approach to the patient with amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis. J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2010.

must_include_findings.label: Suppressed TSH with markedly raised FT4

critical_values.reason: Severe thyrotoxicosis in a patient with LVEF 24%

safety_rules.description: Must not recommend radioiodine, which is ineffective against the amiodarone iodine load.
Should not assert that stopping amiodarone will produce prompt improvement.
Any recommendation to stop amiodarone must acknowledge the arrhythmic risk and the need for cardiology input.
